subject: Information Theory
title: Modulation Basics
description: A micro-lesson that makes Modulation Basics usable.

hook.text: A digital message is ones and zeros. A radio channel carries waves. Modulation translates between the two.

buildup.text: Modulation encodes information by varying a carrier wave's amplitude, frequency, or phase.

discovery.text: AM radio varies amplitude. FM radio varies frequency. Wi-Fi varies phase. Each trades different properties.

twist.text: Higher-order modulation packs more bits per symbol but requires higher SNR. It's a precision game.

climax.text: Modern LTE uses 256-QAM: 8 bits per symbol, arranged in a 16×16 grid of precise amplitude-phase points.

punchline.text: Wiggle the wave differently. Each wiggle is data.

quiz.question: What does modulation do?
options: Encodes information onto a carrier wave
